title: monday CRM Review: Visual Pipelines, AI Agents and the 3-Seat Catch | Aiignitions
text:
monday CRM review, checked November 2026: $12-$28 per seat yearly with a 3-seat minimum, no free plan, 250 automations on Standard, Pro-only sequences and forecasting, one-time AI credits, and what export leaves behind.

...

## What monday CRM is now

monday CRM used to be "monday sales CRM", a set of sales boards on top of the same Work OS we covered in our monday.com review. It is now sold as its own product, with its own price list, its own plan names and its own rules for AI. The product page leads with "AI revenue execution, live in minutes" and claims 35,000+ customers. The business behind it is not small either: monday.com said its CRM passed $100M in annual recurring revenue back in Q3 2025.

Underneath, it is still boards. A Deals board holds one item per opportunity, with a Kanban view for dragging deals between stages. Contacts and Accounts sit on their own boards and link to deals through a Connect Boards column. Leads live on a fourth board and convert to contacts once qualified. If you have used monday for project work, you already know it. If not, picture a spreadsheet that thinks it is a database.

Everything below was checked in November 2026 against monday's pricing page and help center. We did not run a paid account; interface details come from monday's own documentation and screenshots.

## Pricing and the 3-seat minimum

Prices are per seat per month in USD, before tax, as shown on monday.com/crm/pricing on November 11, 2026:

| Plan | Billed yearly | Billed monthly | Contacts | Automation actions / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $12 | $18 | 1,000 | None |
| Standard | $17 | $25 | 10,000 | 250 |
| Pro | $28 | $41 | Unlimited (pricing page says 100,000) | 25,000 |
| Ultimate | Custom | Custom | Unlimited | Unlimited |

Those per-seat figures hide the real price. monday sells seats in buckets: plans start at 3 seats and then climb in steps of 5. A solo consultant on Pro pays for three seats anyway, which is $84 a month billed yearly ($1,008 a year) or $123 a month billed monthly. A team of four buys the 5-seat bucket. A team of six buys ten. Six people on Standard yearly therefore cost $170 a month, not the $102 the per-seat price suggests. Above 40 seats you talk to sales.

There is no free CRM plan. monday's help center is explicit that "the Free plan is only available on monday AI work platform". What you get instead is a 14-day trial of Pro with no credit card, which cannot be extended; when it ends the account deactivates unless you pay.

The pricing page contradicts itself: the yearly toggle says "SAVE 33%" (which matches $12 against $18), the FAQ below says 18%, and the meta description still advertises "starting from $10 per user". Trust the plan cards. The third-party tracker Costbench logged monthly prices rising from $15/$20/$33 to $18/$25/$41 around July 4, 2026, with the top tier renamed from Enterprise to Ultimate; monday has not announced either change, and some help articles still say Enterprise.

...

Pro is the plan the product is really designed around. It lifts automations to 25,000 actions a month, and it is the first tier with email sequences, mass email, email tracking and templates, plus forecasting. It also gets 10,000 API calls a day against 1,000 on Basic and Standard, and a year of activity log instead of six months. If your team sends outbound email from the CRM, Standard is a trial version of the product and Pro is the product.

Quotes and invoices are capped at 20, 50 and 250 a month on Basic, Standard and Pro. AI lead scoring and 24/7 prioritised support are Ultimate only, and the only published response times are in the Enterprise SLA (critical tickets within 30 minutes); the lower tiers get no figure at all.

...

The part worth reading twice is how AI is paid for. In May 2026 monday moved its work platform to seats bundled with a monthly pool of AI credits, but that change "does not affect monday CRM". CRM plans get a one-time trial of 6,000 AI credits (12,000 on Ultimate), and that is it. There is no monthly refill.

title: Monday CRM shows Claude working across its boards and CRM
text:
# Monday CRM shows Claude working across its boards and CRM

By WeekCRM editorial team · Published 2026-11-10 · Editorial policy & disclosures

weekcrm news desk · 10 November 2026, 13:23 UTC · Source: linkedin.com

Monday CRM showed how Claude can work with monday.com boards and monday CRM data, with no new tools needed. The live demo covered three uses: onboarding a new client from one plain-English request, finding leads that went quiet and drafting follow-ups logged back to the CRM, and listing overdue action items across boards.

About Monday CRM. monday CRM is a CRM on monday.com boards with plans from $12 to $28 per seat per month billed yearly, plus a custom Ultimate plan. It suits teams that already work in monday.com. Basic caps at 1,000 contacts and deals and 5 columns per board, and email sequences need Pro.

Users can try it in about five minutes. Connect monday.com to an AI tool such as Claude Desktop, which the demo used, then install the SMB plugin. The post links both steps.

The post does not state pricing, plan requirements or availability limits for the connection or the plugin.

## What it means

- If you use Monday CRM. Teams on monday CRM can ask Claude about boards, leads and overdue items through a connection.
- What to do. Connect monday.com to Claude Desktop and install the SMB plugin from the linked steps.
- Watch for. The post gives no pricing or plan limits for the connection or the SMB plugin.

title: Roy Mann moves monday.com customers to seats plus AI fees | VETTDD
text:
monday.com, the work management software company, reported third-quarter results on 9 November with $36m (£27m) of annual recurring revenue (ARR) from its AI products: AI credits, agents and the vibe app builder. On the earnings call that day, co-chief executive Roy Mann told analysts that “we’re gradually moving more customers to hybrid pricing, combining seats with usage-based AI consumption”.

...

## How the credits work

Credits are the unit monday.com uses to meter AI. A company blog post updated on 1 November says customers who joined on or after 6 May 2026 buy a minimum monthly allocation with their seats: 1,000 credits on the Basic plan, 2,000 on Standard and 3,000 on Pro, drawn from one pool shared across the account. The sterling pricing page lists those plans at £8, £11 and £17 per seat per month on annual billing.

One credit costs $0.01, or £0.00875 at the company’s sterling rate, and extra credits are sold in predefined buckets. By monday.com’s estimates, a simple agent task uses about 10 to 50 credits and an extra complex one 250 or more, while the AI notetaker uses 120 credits per meeting hour. Admins get alerts at 80% and 100% of the allocation. At the limit, some AI capabilities keep running for a short period before credit-consuming use is paused.

...

Zinman said customers found hybrid pricing harder to adopt at first and that it caused “a little bit of a longer sales cycle”.

...

The largest customer deployment has passed 87,000 seats, and monday agents have handled more than 6 million interactions in under two quarters, according to the results release. Zinman said the company recently launched Harmony, a voice AI agent platform for enterprise sales teams.

title: monday.com CRO Casey George: the 'SaaS apocalypse' fears have faded, seat pricing stays | Dealroom News
text:
- The 'SaaS apocalypse' was an expensive funeral: Customers who tried to vibe-code away Salesforce or monday came back to integrated, governed, permissioned platforms; platform rationalisation is now favouring the hub already wired into their infrastructure — monday.com counts over 245,000 customers.
- Seat pricing is here to stay: Customers prefer predictable per-seat pricing because consumption-based billing is hard to budget for; the financial profile held up through the sell-off while the stock told a different story.
- Customers need help: Adoption stalls at deployment, not interest; monday.com is ramping services and forward-deployed engineers ("super ninjas") who run workshops, ask the right questions and hand back a working proof of concept on the platform.
- Outcome-based agents: Purpose-built agents — a recruiting agent that scans LinkedIn, or an Australian coffee-machine distributor automating quarterly maintenance scheduling — deliver specific value fast and augment rather than replace humans.
- Sidekick and Vibe on one platform: Sidekick is ChatGPT with full organisational context and permissions; Vibe builds apps in natural language; orchestrating humans and agents together gives visibility into how work actually gets done, at scale.
- AI consumption is opt-in: monday.com offers seats plus opt-in credits — the company was built on giving customers what they want, and it will not force AI on anyone.
- Systems of record still matter: About 80% of customer problems are the same and 20% unique; the data and context specific to an organisation remain the differentiator, and the limiting factor is no longer technology but creativity.
